methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center cohort of 195 male HCC patients on ICIs with well-defined inclusion/exclusion criteria and L3-SMI measurement by dual radiologists with consensus review. Cox proportional hazards with forward selection (entry P<0.05, removal P<0.10) appropriately identifies independent predictors; SHAP analysis adds interpretability. Limitations: no external validation cohort, male-only to reduce confounding, predominantly early-stage disease (BCLC A/B 70.26%) with low event rate (15% 1-year mortality), median follow-up 14 months insufficient for long-term prognosis.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual retrospective cohort with prognostic outcome (LoE 2b). L3-SMI/BMI identifies practical imaging-based risk marker for HCC-ICI population, addressing clinically relevant stratification need in immunotherapy. However, clinical applicability limited by short follow-up, predominantly early-stage disease, and low event rate; mechanisms for protective muscle effect speculative (myokines, inflammatory modulation suggested but not demonstrated).

reporting_quality.justification: Prognostic biomarker study with comprehensive REMARK-aligned reporting: patient flow documented, baseline characteristics detailed (Table I), univariate/multivariable Cox results clearly presented (Table II with HRs, CIs, p-values), ROC performance summarized (Table III), prognostically relevant figures (risk plots, Kaplan-Meier curves, SHAP importance). L3-SMI measurement methodology transparent (Hounsfield units, muscle groups specified, dual radiologist review protocol). Data availability: no explicit statement regarding raw data repository access or code availability.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel application of L3-SMI/BMI ratio in HCC-ICI cohort with comparison of four muscle indices; L3-SMI established as prognostic in HCC post-resection and other modalities, but ICI-treated cohort and BMI-adjusted ratio represent meaningful extension. Demonstrates that weight adjustment mitigates muscle mass overestimation in obesity, offering practical improvement over standard L3-SMI in this population.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured prognostic study with clear narrative establishing unmet biomarker need in HCC-ICI therapy, comprehensive methods enabling reproducibility, results section integrating risk stratification plots (Fig 2), prognostic curves (Fig 3), and SHAP variable importance (Fig 4). Discussion thoughtfully addresses BMI paradox in ICI literature and mechanisms of protective muscle effect. Minor organizational clarity in methods section but overall publication-ready.

key_strengths: Novel L3-SMI/BMI ratio demonstrates superior predictive performance (AUC 0.86) compared to individual muscle indices, with clear clinical applicability for risk stratification in HCC-ICI population
Rigorous CT measurement methodology with dual radiologist review and consensus protocol minimizes measurement error and enhances reproducibility of skeletal muscle assessment
SHAP analysis provides transparent ranking of variable importance, revealing L3-SMI/BMI as dominant predictor of 1-year mortality and enabling clinician interpretability for decision-making

Appropriate statistical approach with forward Cox regression model selection and separate age-adjusted multivariable analysis, with recognition that low event rate may underestimate biomarker discriminative ability
key_concerns: Single-center retrospective design with selection bias risk; male-only cohort (intentional to reduce confounding) limits generalizability to female HCC patients on immunotherapy

Predominantly early-stage disease (BCLC A/B 70.26%) with low 1-year mortality (15%) and short follow-up (median 14 months) may artificially inflate biomarker performance; insufficient for evaluating long-term prognostic utility
No external validation cohort; findings require independent confirmation in diverse HCC-ICI populations across treatment settings and geographic regions

Mechanisms for protective muscle effect remain speculative (myokines, inflammatory modulation proposed); no mechanistic studies, biomarker validation, or assessment of muscle quality (CT density, texture) provided
chief_reviewer.rationale: Solid prognostic biomarker study with novel L3-SMI/BMI ratio and rigorous CT methodology, but single-center retrospective design, male-only population, predominantly early-stage disease, and lack of external validation limit tier to 3. Appropriate for specialty journals after data availability statement addition.
